headline: Joe Burrow Jersey: The Bengals QB Knocking on the Top 25
title: Joe Burrow Jersey: Bengals QB Knocking on the Top 25
description: Joe Burrow's jersey ranked No. 26 in NFLPA player sales for 2025-26. Why a healthy season could push the Bengals quarterback's No. 9 into the top 25.
body: Shopping for a Joe Burrow jersey means buying into one of the AFC's most dependable reasons to watch on Sunday. The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft, has spent six seasons turning Cincinnati into a regular national-television draw, and his No. 9 has become the franchise's signature look.
## Where his jersey stands

The numbers say Burrow already sells, just not at the very top. He finished No. 26 on the NFL Players Association's year-end list of licensed player merchandise for March 2025 through February 2026, one spot outside the top 25 shown on our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) list. On the union's jersey-only list for March through July 2025, he was No. 21.

Health has been the swing factor. Turf toe surgery limited him to eight games in 2025, when he still threw 17 touchdown passes against five interceptions. He is also a two-time Comeback Player of the Year, in 2021 and 2024, and a three-time Pro Bowler, which says plenty about how he responds to setbacks.
So far in 2026 he has looked like himself, with 428 passing yards against Jacksonville in Week 4 and four touchdown passes in a Week 5 win at Miami.
## What could move him up

Quarterbacks lead jersey sales because they are the face of a franchise, and Burrow's path into the top 25 runs through availability. A full season throwing to Ja'Marr Chase, plus a January run out of a crowded AFC North, would put him back in the prime-time windows that tend to reach casual buyers. That is a projection, not a promise, but few players are a single healthy season away from so much exposure.

headline: Justin Herbert Jersey Sales: Can a Turnaround Lift the No. 10?
title: Justin Herbert Jersey Sales and the Chargers' Hard Start
description: Justin Herbert ranked No. 32 in NFLPA player sales for 2025-26. How the Chargers' 0-6 start and a possible turnaround could shape demand for his jersey.
body: Justin Herbert jersey sales are a useful reminder that merchandise demand is not only about wins. The Los Angeles Chargers quarterback finished No. 32 on the NFL Players Association's year-end merchandise list for March 2025 through February 2026, and he was No. 20 on the union's jersey-only list for March through July 2025.
Those finishes followed a strong 2025. Herbert threw for 3,727 yards and 26 touchdowns, ran for a career-high 498 yards and went 11-5 as a starter before a 16-3 wild-card loss at New England.
## A hard start in 2026

This season has tested that goodwill. The Chargers were 0-6 after a 22-6 loss at Kansas City on Oct. 18, and through five weeks Herbert led the league with seven interceptions. The team publicly shot down trade talk in mid-October.

Why keep an eye on his jersey anyway? Herbert is still a two-time Pro Bowler and the 2020 Offensive Rookie of the Year, the No. 6 overall pick that spring. He also plays in the country's second-largest media market, a platform few quarterbacks get, and his engagement to singer Madison Beer this summer put his name in front of an audience well beyond football.
## What would change the picture

A turnaround is the storyline that would matter most. A quarterback who drags a season back from 0-6 tends to dominate the conversation, and that kind of attention can show up in sales. If it happens, Herbert has a realistic path back toward the top 25 on our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) list. If it doesn't, his No. 10 is more likely to remain a strong regional seller than a national one.

headline: Travis Kelce Jersey: Why the No. 87 Still Sells
title: Travis Kelce Jersey: Why the Chiefs' No. 87 Still Sells
description: Travis Kelce came back for 2026 and ranked No. 29 in NFLPA player sales for 2025-26. Why the Chiefs tight end's No. 87 jersey keeps drawing new buyers.
body: A Travis Kelce jersey is about as close to a safe pick as the NFL offers. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has three Super Bowl rings, 11 Pro Bowl selections and four first-team All-Pro nods, and his No. 87 is one of the most recognizable numbers in the sport.

That recognition shows up in the data. Kelce placed No. 29 on the NFL Players Association's year-end merchandise list covering March 2025 through February 2026, a list that counts all licensed player products, with jerseys leading the way. He did it in a season when the Chiefs went 6-11 and he caught 76 passes for 851 yards.
## One more season

There was real doubt he would play in 2026. Instead, Kelce agreed in March to return to Kansas City, and through six games he had 20 catches for 299 yards and two touchdowns. He was listed as questionable for Week 7 at Seattle with an ankle injury.

His appeal also stretches past the box score. Few active players have his reach with casual fans, and his podcast and pop-culture profile keep him in front of people who rarely sit through a full game. That is exactly the audience that buys a jersey as a gift.
## Why he could climb

What could lift him above No. 29? Every snap at this stage of his career invites the question of how many are left, and the late seasons of likely Hall of Famers often bring a final wave of interest. A Chiefs playoff push would add to it. Fans who want an 87 from his playing days may not want to wait long. The current leaders are on our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) list.

headline: A.J. Brown Patriots Jersey: A New Team and a New Number
title: A.J. Brown Patriots Jersey: New Team, New No. 1 Look
description: A.J. Brown was traded to New England in June and now wears No. 1. Why the Patriots receiver's new jersey could become one of the season's notable sellers.
body: The A.J. Brown Patriots jersey did not exist until this summer. On June 1, Philadelphia traded the star receiver to New England for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder, reuniting him with Mike Vrabel, his former coach in Tennessee. He also changed numbers, trading the No. 11 he wore with the Titans and Eagles for No. 1, his number at Ole Miss.
## A reset for buyers

A trade plus a new number is about as clean a reset as jersey shopping gets. Fans who own a green No. 11 have a reason to buy again, and New England fans now have an established top receiver to pair with quarterback [Drake Maye](/players/drake-maye/), who ranked No. 2 on our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) list.

Brown brings a strong résumé. In 2025 he caught 78 passes for 1,003 yards and seven touchdowns, becoming the first Eagles wide receiver with four straight 1,000-yard seasons, after helping Philadelphia win Super Bowl LIX the season before. He also finished No. 50 on the NFL Players Association's year-end merchandise list for March 2025 through February 2026, counted as an Eagle.
## A bumpy start

His first weeks in New England have been uneven. A high ankle sprain in Week 1 sent him to injured reserve, and in his Oct. 18 home debut he caught three of 10 targets for 27 yards, with three drops, in a 26-19 win over the Jets.

That leaves plenty of season to change the story. A healthy Brown alongside a rising young quarterback could make New England's passing game one of the league's more closely watched, and his first full sales period in Patriots colors is one to keep an eye on.

description: Ja'Marr Chase is a two-time All-Pro but ranked No. 45 in NFLPA player sales for 2025-26. Why the Bengals receiver's jersey has room to climb the rankings.
body: Ja'Marr Chase's jersey ranking shows one of the biggest gaps between performance and merchandise in the NFL. The Cincinnati Bengals receiver has been a first-team All-Pro in each of the last two seasons, yet he finished No. 45 on the NFL Players Association's year-end merchandise list for March 2025 through February 2026. On the union's jersey-only list for March through July 2025, he was No. 44.

On the field, there is no gap at all. Chase won the receiving triple crown in 2024, leading the league in catches, yards and touchdowns, and followed with 125 receptions for 1,412 yards in 2025. He has made five straight Pro Bowls since winning Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2021, and in March 2025 he signed a four-year, $161 million extension, at the time the richest ever for a non-quarterback.
## Why the gap exists

Receivers usually trail quarterbacks in jersey sales, and Cincinnati is one of the NFL's smaller markets. Chase also shares the spotlight with quarterback Joe Burrow, his college teammate, whose No. 9 ranked higher on the same list.
## What could close it

Postseason football is the most direct fix. Chase and Burrow reached Super Bowl LVI together after the 2021 season, and another January run would put the No. 1 jersey in front of millions of viewers who do not follow the Bengals week to week. He returned from a concussion scare in early October with a touchdown at Miami. If his production holds, a climb toward the top 25 shown on our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) list is a realistic target.

title: Derrick Henry Ravens Jersey: Still Selling in Year 11
description: Derrick Henry ranked No. 46 in NFLPA player sales for 2025-26 at age 32. Why the Ravens running back's No. 22 jersey keeps its appeal in his 11th season.
body: Few running backs reach an 11th NFL season, and fewer are still this productive when they do. That is a big part of why a Derrick Henry Ravens jersey keeps finding buyers. Henry finished No. 46 on the NFL Players Association's year-end merchandise list for March 2025 through February 2026, a notable result for a 32-year-old at a position known for short careers.

His 2025 season explains it. Henry ran for 1,595 yards and 16 touchdowns at 5.2 yards per carry in Baltimore, the kind of output usually expected from backs years younger. He has said he has not thought about retirement, and through five games of 2026 he had 476 rushing yards and seven total touchdowns.
## A milestone in reach

Entering Week 6, Henry was one rushing touchdown short of 40 with the Ravens, to go with 90 from his years in Tennessee. He was held scoreless for the first time this season in a 13-10 loss at Cleveland on Oct. 18.

His résumé already makes a strong Hall of Fame case: the 2015 Heisman Trophy, the 2020 AP Offensive Player of the Year award and five Pro Bowl selections. Few active players can match that mix of college and professional honors.
## Two fan bases, one number

Henry has worn No. 22 in both Tennessee and Baltimore, so his jersey carries meaning for two fan bases. A deep Ravens playoff run would give him one of the biggest stages of his career, and late-career stars often draw new buyers when they do. headline: Brock Bowers Jersey: A Record-Setting Tight End's Next Step
title: Brock Bowers Jersey: The Raiders Tight End's Next Step
description: Brock Bowers set the NFL rookie catch record in 2024. Why the Raiders tight end's No. 89 jersey could return to the sales lists with a healthy 2026 season.
secondaryKeywords: who could crack the top-selling jersey rankings next
body: Only a handful of tight ends show up on jersey sales lists in a given year, which makes Brock Bowers an interesting case. The Las Vegas Raiders tight end set the NFL record for catches by a rookie with 112 in 2024, set the rookie tight end mark with 1,194 yards and was named first-team All-Pro. His jersey was No. 46 on the NFL Players Association's jersey-only sales list for March through July 2025.

That early momentum stalled. Bowers caught 64 passes for 680 yards and seven touchdowns in 12 games in 2025 before a knee injury ended his season in December, and he did not appear on the NFLPA's year-end top 50 for March 2025 through February 2026. He still made the Pro Bowl.
## Breakout, part two

This season has brought more maintenance, including a meniscus trim in early September and a hamstring and calf issue on the Week 7 injury report. He was a full participant in practice on Oct. 22, a good sign for the weeks ahead.

His jersey case is about what a full, healthy season could look like. Bowers is a young tight end used like a receiver, with record production already on his résumé. The Raiders also have second-year running back [Ashton Jeanty](/jerseys/ashton-jeanty-jersey/), whose own jersey started fast, and two young stars give national broadcasts more reasons to feature Las Vegas.
## The path back

If Bowers stays on the field, the No. 89 has the ingredients to rejoin the conversation on lists like our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) rankings. Tight ends who become a quarterback's first read tend to pile up the kind of numbers that make highlight shows, and that is how a position that rarely sells jerseys produces an exception.

headline: Baker Mayfield Jersey: Tampa Bay's Comeback Story Sells
title: Baker Mayfield Jersey: Tampa Bay's Comeback Story Sells
description: Baker Mayfield ranked No. 28 in NFLPA player sales for 2025-26 and signed a $165 million extension. Why the Bucs quarterback's No. 6 jersey keeps selling.
body: A Baker Mayfield jersey sells better than many fans might expect. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback finished No. 28 on the NFL Players Association's year-end merchandise list for March 2025 through February 2026, and he was No. 25 on the union's jersey-only list for March through July 2025. For a player who was once written off, that is quite a turnaround.
## The comeback story

Mayfield went first overall to Cleveland in 2018, and after short stints in Carolina and Los Angeles he found stability in Tampa Bay, earning Pro Bowl selections in 2023 and 2024. That kind of career arc builds loyalty, and his fiery, emotional style has made him easy to root for.

The Bucs made their commitment clear on Sept. 8, signing him to a three-year, $165 million extension. In 2025 he threw for 3,693 yards and 26 touchdowns against 11 interceptions, with the Bucs going 8-9 in his starts.
## An untimely injury

The timing of his latest setback is hard on Tampa Bay. Mayfield dislocated his right thumb and missed a third straight game in Week 6, with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starting in his place. His return date had not been confirmed as of Oct. 23.

A healthy return to lead a playoff push would put the No. 6 back on national highlight shows, and with his new contract, fans buying it now are buying a quarterback expected to be in Tampa for years. He sits just outside the top 25 shown on our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) list, close enough that a strong finish could matter.

headline: Josh Jacobs Packers Jersey: A Return With Questions
title: Josh Jacobs Packers Jersey: A Return With Open Questions
description: Josh Jacobs returns to the Packers after six games on the Commissioner's Exempt List. What his comeback means for fans weighing his No. 8 Green Bay jersey.
body: Josh Jacobs returns to the Green Bay Packers' lineup this week under very different circumstances than a year ago. The running back, who wears No. 8 in Green Bay, began 2026 on the NFL's Commissioner's Exempt List after a May arrest in Wisconsin and missed the first six games. The charges were reduced to two misdemeanors, he pleaded no contest in September, and he was expected to make his season debut against Detroit in Week 7. The league's personal-conduct review was still open as of Oct. 21.
## The football case

Before this season, Jacobs was one of the most productive backs in football. He led the NFL with 1,653 rushing yards in 2022, earning first-team All-Pro honors, and he has made three Pro Bowls. In 2025 he ran for 13 touchdowns in 15 games for Green Bay.

Jacobs did not appear on the NFL Players Association's year-end top 50 for licensed player merchandise covering March 2025 through February 2026, even as Packers teammates [Jordan Love](/players/jordan-love/) and [Micah Parsons](/players/micah-parsons/) ranked in the top 10 of our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) list.
## What fans are weighing

For buyers, the honest answer is that his jersey's outlook depends on more than football. The result of the NFL's review and how he handles his return will shape how fans respond, and some will choose to wait for that clarity before buying.

On the field, he still offers a proven three-down skill set and plenty of experience for a team in a crowded NFC North race. A strong second half for a contender is the scenario in which interest could recover, but it is far from certain.

body: Terry McLaurin's season ended on Oct. 19, when the Washington Commanders receiver tore the patellar tendon in his left knee in the first quarter of a Monday night game against San Francisco. ## A fan favorite's jersey

For Washington fans, the injury hit a player who has been a constant through years of change. McLaurin was a third-round pick, 76th overall, in 2019, and he outplayed that draft slot almost from the start. He made Pro Bowls in 2022 and 2024, was a second-team All-Pro in 2024 and signed a three-year, $96 million extension in August 2025 after a holdout.

Long before the team's resurgence with quarterback [Jayden Daniels](/players/jayden-daniels/), McLaurin was one of the main reasons to watch Washington. Daniels now ranks No. 5 on our [Top Selling NFL Jerseys](/top-selling-nfl-jerseys/) list, and McLaurin has been one of his most trusted targets.

The past year has been less straightforward. Thomas caught 48 passes for 707 yards and two touchdowns in 2025, and his 10 drops were tied for second-most in the league. ## The upside case

A Brian Thomas Jr. jersey is a bet on talent over recent results. He is fast, he is young, and he has already shown he can produce at a Pro Bowl level, something few receivers manage as rookies. A bounce-back stretch would revive the excitement from his rookie year, and if his situation in Jacksonville changes, a fresh start could put his jersey in front of an entirely new audience.
Either way, the next few months will decide whether his No. 7 becomes a trend or a footnote. This is one to revisit after the trade deadline.

The Jets' challenge is winning enough to give Hall that stage. In the New York market, even a modest playoff push draws heavy coverage, and a healthy Hall would be central to it alongside receiver [Garrett Wilson](/jerseys/garrett-wilson-jersey/). With his contract settled, his No. 20 is a jersey fans can buy knowing he is expected to stay in green for years.
